newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-JONES OVERWHELMS BRANNON, QUARTEY STOPS CARR.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-JONES OVERWHELMS BRANNON, QUARTEY STOPS CARR.

text.p: Roy Jones Jr, called by many the best pound-for-pound fighter in the world, impressively kept his IBF super middleweight title Friday, stopping a game but thoroughly out-classed Bryant Brannon in the second round.

Jones, 27, retained his International Boxing Federation crown after dropping Brannon twice in the second round before referee Ron Lipton, who moments before the end had ignored Jones' gesture to stop Brannon's beating, waved off the bout at 2:23 of the round with Brannon on the canvas at Madison Square Garden.

Lipton "should have stopped the fight when I told him after the first knockout in the second round," said Jones, 32-0, who had also put Brannon down in the opening round of the scheduled-12 round fight.
Brannon, now 16-1, went down early in the second round from a combination ending with a left hook. The final knockdown came after a flurry of blows ended with a right hand.
"I tried to speed it up a little bit, I didn't want to hurt him, I just wanted to hit him enough to get him down," said Jones.
Earlier, undefeated Ike Quartey of Ghana retained his World Boxing Association welterweight title with a 12-round majority decision victory over American challenger Oba Carr.
Judge Luis Rivera of Puerto Rico scored it 116-109, judge Jose Laurino of Uruguay 117-107, and judge Gonzalo Riveras of Venezuela had it 112-112.
It was a bruising bout between two hard punchers with Quartey (33-0) landing most punches. Carr (39-2) was cut under his right eye and his left eye was nearly shut.

Brannon, the IBF's top ranked challenger, proved to be just another in a lineup of outclassed foes who have failed to give Jones a real challenge. Jones, in four of his five title defences since outpointing American James Toney to win the title two years ago, has not gone past the sixth round.
Before his last bout, the supremely confident Jones played in a minor league professional basketball game in the afternoon before stopping Canadian Eric Lucas in the 11th round.
This time, just an hour before the opening bell, Jones sat in the middle of the ring and took part in a question and answer session withjournalists and fans.
Brannon, 29, who served five years in prison for robbery and survived six gunshot wounds, at least was tough as long as he was standing.
Proceeds from the fight, after deductions for expenses, went to three New York City charities, promoters said.
